chift_routes.one_line: Map to POST /invoices.sales.new (customer_*) or POST /invoices.purchases.new (supplier_*), with Type 0 for an invoice and 1 for a credit note, using multipart/form-data when a PDF is attached. First resolve FolderId (D7), the DaybookId per invoice_type with the refund fallback 250→200 / 150→100 (D1), a found-or-created CompanyId (partner_info.account_number = company SearchKey, find → set role flag → create, D10), the account search keys, and the cost schema/section search keys from the per-folder analytics cache (D8). Main caveats: Horus has no VAT-code entity, so tax_code is decoded from the connector's synthetic catalogue (S-…/P-… grammar, D2); Number must be numeric, with no auto-numbering, no idempotency key and no invoice delete (DocumentNo pre-check, D12); reference and customer_memo share the header Comment (D3). Horus returns only the book entry Id, so the response is rebuilt from the echo plus GET /book-entries.info (folder-checked, D13), and POST /account-histories.list only when line-level data is needed (EUR amounts, D4).

summary:
Horus has two native write endpoints for this route. POST /invoices.sales.new takes customer_invoice (Type=0) and customer_refund (Type=1). POST /invoices.purchases.new takes supplier_invoice (Type=0) and supplier_refund (Type=1). Both accept header totals, VAT-qualified lines, multi-schema cost lines, a currency and the PDF in one multipart call. Horus's own posting guide lists the four prerequisites the connector must resolve first: FolderId, a 200/250 or 100/150 DaybookId, a found-or-created CompanyId, and the account search keys.

One Chift call therefore becomes several Horus calls:
- **Folder (D7):** folder_id is required when the connection has more than one selected folder; otherwise the single selected folder, or the single folder from folders.list, is used.
- **Cached lookups per folder:** daybooks (D1 filter: customer_invoice → 200; customer_refund → 250, else 200; supplier_invoice → 100; supplier_refund → 150, else 100; exactly one candidate or 400 'journal_id required'), accounts, the analytics cache (cost schemas + cost sections including inactive ones, D8), fiscal years (closure dates and IsClosed) and the folder.
- **Partner:** partner_id is folder-checked with companies.info (D13). partner_info is treated as the company SearchKey (A, D10): companies.list, then companies.update to set a missing IsCustomer/IsSupplier flag, or companies.new if no match.
- **Duplicate pre-check (D12):** book-entries.list on DocumentNo whenever invoice_number is supplied, and again before any retry. Horus documents no uniqueness or idempotency key and offers no invoice delete.
- **The create call itself.**
- **Read-back (skipped when ignore_accounting_id=true):** create returns only {Id}, so GET /book-entries.info?Id=… reads the entry back in one call with no period and its Folder.Id is checked (D13). POST /account-histories.list filtered on BookEntryId is added only when line-level data is needed (the EUR partner-line amount of a foreign-currency invoice per D4, the partner collective account).

The biggest risk is VAT. Chift sends tax_code as 'the Id of the Tax Code', but Horus has no VAT-code entity. Each line needs TaxRate + TaxOrigin + TaxType (purchases add TaxKind/TaxCondition/TaxConditionValue), and the valid combinations are in reference files that were not provided. The connector therefore owns a synthetic VAT-code catalogue with one canonical id grammar shared with GET vat-codes and get_invoices (D2): 'S-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}' (+ '-{TaxCountryCode}' for OSS) and 'P-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}-{TaxKind}-{TaxCondition}-{TaxConditionValue}'.

Other risks:
- Per-plan percentages must become joint cost-line amounts (maximum 8 schemas), rounded with the largest-remainder method; Free schemas are excluded in v1 (D8).
- invoice_number must be numeric.
- API entries are unconfirmed by default so the accountant can review them. posted maps to Confirmed=true unless the per-consumer 'always push unconfirmed' setting is on (D12).
- Credit notes may fall back to a 200/100 daybook (D1), which Horus has not confirmed it accepts.
- reference and customer_memo share the header Comment ('{reference} | {customer_memo}', D3), so reference is lost as a structured field.
- Several Chift fields have no Horus field: withholding_tax, nl_payment_terms_split, start/end/delivery dates, force_financial_period, payment_term_id, and line quantity/unit price.

Operationally, every retry must first run the duplicate pre-check, token refreshes must be serialised (refresh tokens are single-use), and all write tests must use a test folder, because the API works on the license's real data.
verdict_rationale:
The capability is native. Horus has dedicated sale and purchase invoice endpoints with credit-note support, lines, VAT, multi-axis analytics, currency and the PDF in one call, and the Guide: Posting sales & purchase invoices describes exactly this use case. Under the shared verdict calibration (D11: workaround = feasible, but needs extra per-request calls, emulated behaviour, or loses capabilities clients rely on), the verdict is workaround, not supported, for six reasons:
1. The required Chift tax_code has no Horus counterpart. A combination of enums must be emulated from a connector-maintained catalogue with the D2 id grammar, and the accepted-combination files are not among the admissible sources.
2. Every reference must be resolved or validated through other endpoints: folder (D7), daybook per invoice_type with the refund fallback (D1), partner found, flagged or created (D10) and folder-checked (D13), accounts, and cost schemas/sections from the per-folder cache (D8). Analytics must be converted from percentages to amounts.
3. Numbering and idempotency need an emulated pre-check through book-entries.list (D12). Horus has no AutoGenerateNumber on invoices, no documented uniqueness rule, and no invoice delete to undo a duplicate.
4. The Chift response must be rebuilt from echoed values plus read-back calls, because create returns only {Id}. GET /book-entries.info reads the header back in one call by Id, but line-level data (EUR amounts under D4, partner collective account, booked VAT and cost detail) still needs the period-bounded account-histories.list.
5. Several Chift fields are lost or rejected: reference as a structured field (merged into Comment, D3), withholding_tax, nl_payment_terms_split, accrual and delivery dates, force_financial_period, payment_term_id, quantity/unit_price/unit_of_measure, and Free-schema analytics (D8).
6. Status mapping has business weight: Horus API entries are unconfirmed by default so the accountant can review them, hence the per-consumer 'always push unconfirmed' setting (D12).

The result will contain the generated book entry's id."; Type: "0 for an invoice, 1 for a credit note"; Guide: Data model: daybook "Sale / Sale credit note 200 / 250" → "invoices.sales.new"

horus_endpoints.role: Creates the purchase invoice (supplier_invoice: Type=0) or purchase credit note (supplier_refund: Type=1), with the same JSON and multipart variants. Purchase lines add TaxKind/TaxCondition/TaxConditionValue, VehicleId and PersonalShare. Number is nullable here.

A license holds several folders. Also returns WithAnalytics and Legislation (BE/LU).

Exactly one candidate daybook must remain, otherwise 400 'journal_id required'. When journal_id is given, the cached, folder-scoped list validates that the daybook exists in the folder (which also enforces D13) and that its Type belongs to the invoice side (200/250 for customer_*, 100/150 for supplier_*). Also gives the daybook SearchKey (e.g. VEN), which the BookEntryNumber format uses.

call_sequence: 0. Connection context (Chift-internal). consumer_id → the stored Horus connection: one per license, holding api_url, access token, refresh token and expiry. Access tokens last 1 hour. Refresh proactively a few minutes before expiry, under a per-connection lock, and persist the new token pair before using it, because refresh tokens are single-use (Guide: Token lifecycle). Send Content-Encoding: gzip (Guide: Making requests) and ignore unknown response properties (Guide: Changes & versioning). FolderId (D7): folder_id when given; if it is null and exactly one folder was selected at activation, that folder; if no selection is stored, the single folder returned by POST /folders.list {Mode: 0}; otherwise 400 'folder_id required'.

1. Chift-side validation, before any Horus call:
- total = untaxed_amount + tax_amount on the header and on each line.
- Header totals = sum of the lines; otherwise invoice_correction is needed.
- Analytic percentages are integers summing to 100 per plan, with at most 8 plans.
- Every tax_code (and correction tax code) is a D2 catalogue id with the prefix of the invoice side (S- for customer_*, P- for supplier_*).
- The PDF type is one of Pdf/Xml/CODA/SODA/jpg/jpeg/png.
- Reject unsupported inputs with 400/422: withholding_tax, nl_payment_terms_split, a force_financial_period that differs from the invoice_date month, a currency outside the Horus enum, a non-numeric invoice_number.
2. If regroup_lines='true' (the default), merge lines that share (account_number, tax_code, analytic_distribution), summing untaxed_amount, tax_amount and total.

3. Reference data, loaded once and cached per folder (Guide: Reading accounting data):
- POST /daybooks.list: resolve DaybookId with the D1 filter (customer_invoice [200]; customer_refund [250], else [200]; supplier_invoice [100]; supplier_refund [150], else [100]); exactly one candidate, otherwise 400 'journal_id required'. A given journal_id must be in this folder-scoped list with a Type of the invoice side.
- POST /accounts.list: exact search key, Inactive=false, optionally IsSummary=false.
- Analytics cache (D8): POST /cost-schemas.list, then POST /cost-sections.list per List-type schema with Filter.IncludeInactive = true. Map GUID ids to search keys; read Mandatory and CostSectionType.
- POST /fiscal-years.list, then GET /fiscal-years.info: fiscal year bounds, closure dates and IsClosed for invoice_date. Horus recommends this closure check (Guide: Data model).
- GET /folders.info: WithAnalytics, Language, CountryCode.

4. Partner (Guide: Managing customers & suppliers: 'find or create the company first').
- partner_id set: CompanyId = partner_id. Guard with GET /companies.info (cached): Data.Folder.Id must equal folder_id, otherwise 400 (D13); check IsCustomer/IsSupplier for the invoice side.
- partner_id null and partner_info set (D10): SearchKey = account_number sanitised with create_client's rules. POST /companies.list (FolderId, Filter.SearchKey), then post-filter on an exact match in the same folder. If the match lacks IsCustomer (customer_*) or IsSupplier (supplier_*), POST /companies.update with CompanyId + that flag only (never "" values). If no match, POST /companies.new with create_client's required-field rules (LanguageCode = folder Language per D9, CountryCode = folder CountryCode, IsVatLiable=false, optional ExternalReference), and use the returned Id as CompanyId.
- Both null: reject, because CompanyId is required.

5. VAT (D2): decode each lines[].tax_code, and the correction tax code, through the connector's catalogue:
- Sales 'S-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}' → TaxRate, TaxOrigin, TaxType; OSS ids (TaxOrigin=13) carry a fifth component → TaxCountryCode.
- Purchases 'P-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}-{TaxKind}-{TaxCondition}-{TaxConditionValue}' → the six fields, 'x' → null.
An id not in the catalogue → 422. Check the decoded rate against lines[].tax_rate.

6. Numbering and duplicate pre-check (D12). Number = int(invoice_number).
- invoice_number set: POST /book-entries.list (FolderId, DaybookId, fiscal-year months, Filter.DocumentNo=Number) before creating. Unconfirmed entries are included by default. If an entry exists, return 409 Conflict (or the existing entry, per Chift policy). This follows Horus's advice to reconcile on daybook + entry number.
- invoice_number null: a draft gets Number=0. A posted sale gets max(DocumentNo)+1 from the same call (assumption, race risk) or is rejected. A posted purchase gets null (nullable).

7. Build the Horus body.
- Header: Type, Number, Date, DueDate, CompanyId, totals, PaymentReferences, PaymentMode, CurrencyCode/CurrencyRate, OverrideTaxAmounts=true, AllowUnbalanced=false.
- Comment (D3): '{reference}', '{reference} | {customer_memo}' or '| {customer_memo}'.
- Confirmed (D12): false for draft; true for posted unless the per-consumer 'always push unconfirmed' setting is on.
- InvoiceLines with CostLines: percentages become amounts as a product of combinations across plans, rounded with the largest-remainder method so the cost lines sum exactly to BaseAmount (D8).
- Append an invoice_correction line when header and lines differ.

8. Create: POST /invoices.sales.new (customer_*) or POST /invoices.purchases.new (supplier_*). Without a PDF, use application/json. With a PDF, use multipart/form-data: file = the base64-decoded bytes, body = the JSON as a plain text form field, including FileName with its extension. Error handling (Guide: Responses & errors):
- 400: never retry as-is. Map to Chift 400/422 and surface ErrorType and Details.
- 404: map to Chift 404.
- 401: refresh once under the lock and retry. If the refresh fails, mark the connection disconnected.
- 403: map to Chift 400 'folder not accessible with this connection' (D7).
- 500 or timeout: before any retry, re-run the step-6 DocumentNo pre-check (D12), because Horus has no idempotency key and no invoice delete. Then retry with exponential backoff. Never auto-retry a Number=0 draft.
9. If ignore_accounting_id=true: return the echoed request plus id = the Horus Id right away. Horus is synchronous, so the Id is already known.

10. Otherwise, read back with GET /book-entries.info?Id=<Id>: one call by Id, with no FolderId, DaybookId or period. Check Data.Folder.Id = folder_id (D13). It gives DocumentNo, Confirmed, Date, LastModifiedDate (last_updated_on), CompanyDetail (Company, DueDate, TotalAmount, TurnoverAmount, TaxAmount, RemarkPayment), Daybook and Document. Its CompanyDetail amounts are assumed EUR (D4) and are never returned under a foreign currency code. Add POST /account-histories.list (FolderId, the fiscal-year period, Filter.BookEntryId=Id, IncludeVatDetail, IncludeCostDetail, IncludeCompanyDetail, optionally Include='CompanyDetail.Company') only when a field needs line data: the EUR partner-line amount and applied CurrencyRate of a foreign-currency invoice, the partner collective account, or booked VAT/cost detail. If that list returns nothing, fall back to GET /account-histories.info for each AccountHistories[].Id from book-entries.info. Optionally call GET /documents.info with Document.Id for the file name. If the read-back fails, never re-create the invoice: return the Id with echoed values.

11. Assemble InvoiceItemOutMultiAnalyticPlans from the request echo, the resolved Ids and the read-back values (see the response mappings). Currency rule (D4): amounts are the echoed invoice-currency amounts with the echoed currency; accounting_info.main_currency_total = the EUR partner-line amount; EUR amounts are never paired with a foreign currency code.

field_mappings.rule: Horus has no VAT-code Id. The connector owns a VAT catalogue built from the Horus accepted-combination files (not provided; requested from Horus) and exposes it through Chift GET vat-codes with ONE canonical id grammar (D2), used identically for decoding here and for encoding in get_invoices. Sales: 'S-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}', plus '-{TaxCountryCode}' only for OSS lines (TaxOrigin = 13); example 'S-21-0-0'. Purchases: 'P-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}-{TaxKind}-{TaxCondition}-{TaxConditionValue}', with 'x' for an unused component; example 'P-21-2-0-0-1-true'. Decoding: the id must exist in the catalogue (otherwise 422) and carry the prefix of the invoice side (S- for customer_*, P- for supplier_*); its components fill TaxRate/TaxOrigin/TaxType (+ TaxKind/TaxCondition/TaxConditionValue for purchases, null for 'x'; + TaxCountryCode for OSS sales). The Chift scope nat/eu/int published in GET vat-codes follows TaxType 0/1/2. Horus VatCode is never accepted or returned as the Chift tax_code (D2). Optional (A): human labels for the catalogue entries (labels only, never ids) by mining the distinct VatDetail combinations already used in the folder (account-histories.list).

field_mappings.rule: Convert the per-plan percentage splits into Horus cost lines: an amount plus one Costs entry per schema, with up to 8 per cost line. One plan: one CostLine per analytic account. The sum of CostLines.Amount must equal BaseAmount, which the D8 largest-remainder rounding guarantees. Maximum 8 schemas. Leave CostDistributionKey null (cost lines take precedence anyway). Plans and sections are resolved only from the per-folder D8 cache. Reject (422) a distribution when the folder has WithAnalytics=false, or when a plan is a Free schema (CostSectionType 900), which is excluded from Chift analytics in v1 (D8).

field_mappings.rule: Each CostLine row amount = BaseAmount × product(pct/100) over the plans of that row. horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: InvoiceLines[].TaxCountryCode (sales, needed for OSS TaxOrigin=13)
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: Fifth component of the D2 OSS sales code S-{TaxRate}-13-{TaxType}-{TaxCountryCode}; shipping_country is only a cross-check. Omitted on non-OSS lines.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: InvoiceLines[].CostLines[].Amount (required inside CostLines)
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: BaseAmount × product of the plan percentages / 100, rounded with the largest-remainder method on the per-line product allocation (D8), so the cost lines sum exactly to BaseAmount.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: FileName (required when a document is attached)
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: pdf_name, with an extension ensured; fallback '<invoice_number or uuid>.pdf'.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: multipart fields 'file' and 'body' (required in the multipart variant)
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: file = the base64-decoded pdf bytes. body = the same JSON object as the application/json variant, sent as a plain text form field. Horus specifies no content type for the part; the guides show curl -F 'body={...}' and a Postman 'body field of type Text'.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: companies.new required fields in the partner_info flow: SearchKey, Name, IsCustomer, IsSupplier, IsVatLiable, LanguageCode, CountryCode
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: create_client's required-field rules (D10): SearchKey = partner_info.account_number sanitised with create_client's SearchKey rules (unique within the folder); Name = account_name; IsCustomer = invoice_type in customer_*; IsSupplier = invoice_type in supplier_*; IsVatLiable = false (no source; flag as a data-quality warning); LanguageCode = GET /folders.info → Language (D9 write-side fallback, sent as-is even when 'XX'); CountryCode = GET /folders.info → CountryCode; optional ExternalReference = a Chift-side key.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: A

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: Support call (partner_info, D10): POST /companies.update → CompanyId * + IsCustomer or IsSupplier
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: CompanyId = the Id of the company matched by SearchKey; set only the missing flag to true (IsCustomer for customer_*, IsSupplier for supplier_*); every other field null or omitted, never "".
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: Support call (D8 cache): POST /cost-sections.list → CostSchemaId *, Filter.IncludeInactive
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: CostSchemaId = each List-type (CostSectionType 100) schema Id from cost-schemas.list; Filter.IncludeInactive = CONSTANT true so inactive sections can be rejected explicitly with 422.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: Support calls: POST /book-entries.list DaybookId + StartMonth/StartYear/EndMonth/EndYear; POST /account-histories.list StartMonth/StartYear/EndMonth/EndYear
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: DaybookId as resolved. Period = the bounds of the fiscal year containing invoice_date (POST /fiscal-years.list Filter.Dates=[invoice_date]). This is safer than the invoice month in case Horus assigns a different accounting month.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: Support call: GET /fiscal-years.info Id
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: Data[].Id of the fiscal year returned by POST /fiscal-years.list Filter.Dates=[invoice_date]; cached.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: Support call (alternative sales read-back): GET /invoices.sales.outstanding.info Id + BookEntryId
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: Id = FolderId (deduced: the guide requires FolderId, and Id is the only remaining parameter); BookEntryId = the Id returned by create.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: Support call (read-back): GET /book-entries.info Id; fallback GET /account-histories.info Id
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: book-entries.info Id = the Id returned by invoices.*.new; its Data.Folder.Id must equal folder_id (D13). account-histories.info Id = each AccountHistories[].Id returned by book-entries.info. Only Id is documented for either call: no FolderId or period.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: F

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: [optional, decision needed] OverrideTaxAmounts
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: CONSTANT true, so Horus books the issued invoice's exact VAT (no recomputation from base × rate).
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: A

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: [optional, decision needed] AllowUnbalanced
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: CONSTANT false (never force unbalanced entries).
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: [optional] Discount, MatchNo, PersonalShare (purchases), CostDistributionKey
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: null; Chift has no source for any of them.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: D

horus_required_without_chift_source.horus_field: [optional] VehicleId (purchases, header or line)
horus_required_without_chift_source.how_to_fill: null by default. Optional per-consumer default vehicle (from POST /vehicles.list) for accounts that require one. Whether Horus rejects a missing VehicleId is undocumented.
horus_required_without_chift_source.label: A

limitations.description: No VAT-code entity or VAT-code list endpoint appears among the 72 documented endpoints. Invoice lines need TaxRate + TaxOrigin + TaxType (+ TaxKind/TaxCondition/TaxConditionValue for purchases), checked against external reference files of accepted combinations. VatCode/VatHeading appear only as read-only output (account-histories VatDetail), where TaxCondition has an extra value '4 = Article' that the purchase input does not accept (enum[0, 1, 2, 3]). Accounts carry VAT settings (VatRate/VatNat) that can help default or validate a decoded combination.
limitations.impact: Chift GET vat-codes must be emulated from a connector-maintained catalogue with the canonical D2 id grammar (S-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}[-{TaxCountryCode}] / P-{TaxRate}-{TaxOrigin}-{TaxType}-{TaxKind}-{TaxCondition}-{TaxConditionValue}), and lines[].tax_code is decoded from it. The catalogue must be maintained whenever Horus changes its accepted combinations, and the combination files are not among the admissible sources. Read-side asymmetry: VatDetail has no TaxKind, so get_invoices returns tax_code = null for purchase combinations that differ only by TaxKind (D2); a purchase tax_code written here may not survive the round trip.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Invoice Number is numeric (Chift invoice_number is a string). Invoices have no AutoGenerateNumber field, unlike miscellaneous operations, banks and financials. No uniqueness constraint, idempotency key or external reference field is documented for invoices.
limitations.impact: Non-numeric invoice numbers are rejected. Auto-numbering for posted sales must be emulated (max+1, with a race risk). Idempotency must be emulated with a book-entries.list DocumentNo pre-check that returns 409.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: No dedicated field for reference (the supplier's invoice number on purchases). Header free text is limited to Comment and PaymentReferences.
limitations.impact: reference is merged into Comment with the D3 convention ('{reference} | {customer_memo}', or '| {customer_memo}' without reference), so later GET invoices cannot filter on it and can only parse it back from the header Comment, whose location on read is undocumented. Comment length limits are undocumented (?).
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Several Chift inputs have no Horus field: force_financial_period, withholding_tax, nl_payment_terms_split, start_date/end_date, delivery_date, payment_term_id, and line unit_price/quantity/unit_of_measure.
limitations.impact: These are either rejected (force_financial_period when it differs from the invoice month, withholding_tax, nl_payment_terms_split) or ignored with a warning (accrual/delivery dates, payment term, quantity/price). Clients relying on them lose that data.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: Horus analytics are amounts on joint cost-line combinations (CostLines[].Amount + Costs[] per schema), not per-plan percentages. A folder can have at most 8 cost schemas, and each cost history at most 8 cost sections. Schemas can be Mandatory or Free (CostSectionType 900).
limitations.impact: Percentages must be converted to amounts with largest-remainder cent rounding (D8). Several split plans require a Cartesian product, which assumes the plans are independent. A read-back cannot reproduce integer percentages exactly. Free schemas (CostSectionType 900) are excluded from Chift analytics in v1 (D8), so their values cannot be posted through the connector.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Currency: EUR is implicit (null). Only 32 other ISO codes are accepted. The folder must be configured for currencies, and no API field exposes that setting. The CurrencyRate direction is undocumented, and so is the currency of the invoice amounts.
limitations.impact: Invoices in other currencies are rejected. A rate in the wrong direction would misstate EUR amounts, so validate with Horus before go-live. D4 assumption: account-history Debit/Credit and CompanyDetail amounts are in EUR, so the response pairs echoed invoice-currency amounts with the echoed currency and returns the EUR partner-line amount only as main_currency_total.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Create returns only {Id} (Guide: Responses & errors). GET /book-entries.info reads the entry back by that Id with no period, but it returns entry-level data only: lines appear as references (AccountHistories: Type + Id), without amounts, VAT, cost detail, currency or account search keys. Line data comes from account-histories.list, which needs FolderId and mandatory period parameters, or from GET /account-histories.info at one call per line.
limitations.impact: In the common case, the full Chift response needs echoed values plus 1 read-back call by Id (last_updated_on, status, DocumentNo, header totals, document). The actual EUR totals of a foreign-currency invoice and the partner collective account still need a second, period-bounded call (0-1 extra).
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: invoices.*.update is a full replacement: it needs every creation-required field, returns a NEW book entry Id, and deletes the original attachment.
limitations.impact: Chift invoice ids do not survive Horus updates, for example a draft confirmed later through the API. Any later status change or correction means re-sending the full payload and the PDF, and the Chift id and attachments_info change. Clients storing ids must be warned. Horus recommends reconciling on daybook + entry number rather than the Id alone.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Credit notes use Type=1, but the sources do not say whether amounts must be positive, or whether a credit note may be posted into a 200/100 daybook (or an invoice into 250/150). The posting guide does not tie Type to a daybook type. The connector applies the D1 fallback (customer_refund 250 → 200, supplier_refund 150 → 100), which relies on that undocumented acceptance.
limitations.impact: A wrong sign or a refused daybook gives a Horus 400 or reversed postings. Credit notes posted into a 200/100 daybook can be told apart on read only by the partner-line sign (D1, get_invoices). Needs Horus confirmation before go-live.

limitations.description: A single DueDate per invoice; no instalments.
limitations.impact: due_dates[] in the response always has exactly one element.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Accepted attachment types are documented for all upload routes, invoices.*.new multipart included: Pdf, Xml, CODA, SODA, .jpg/.jpeg/.png (F). No size limit is documented.
limitations.impact: The connector can reject unsupported types before calling, but it cannot pre-check size. Large files may fail with an undocumented error that must be surfaced.

limitations.description: Confirmed means confirmed by the accountant. API entries are unconfirmed by default precisely so the accountant can review them in Horus Office. The Chift default status is 'posted'.
limitations.impact: Mapping posted to Confirmed=true bypasses the fiduciary's review. D12: offer the per-consumer setting 'always push unconfirmed' (recommended where the accountant must review API entries); which default fits fiduciary clients is an open product decision.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Horus legislations are BE and LU only, and the TaxOrigin labels are Belgian/Luxembourgish tax categories (e.g. 'Prestation hors Belgique', 'Prestations hors Luxembourg').
limitations.impact: Non-BE/LU tax scenarios cannot be expressed, and NL-specific Chift fields have no meaning here.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: The API has no invoice delete or cancel endpoint. The only book-entry delete is book-entries.miscellaneous-operations.delete, which works only on unconfirmed miscellaneous operations created through the API.
limitations.impact: The connector cannot undo a wrongly pushed or duplicated invoice, or roll back a multi-step flow (e.g. a failed fallback PDF attach); the accountant must fix it in Horus Office. That is why the duplicate pre-check before any retry is critical. The connector can never produce Chift status 'cancelled'.
limitations.label: D

limitations.description: All requests, writes included, run against the license's real database. No sandbox environment is documented.
limitations.impact: Connector development, QA and certification must use a dedicated test license or test folder. Because invoices cannot be deleted, test invoices remain.
limitations.label: F

limitations.description: Neither the API reference nor the guides document pagination, rate limits or the ErrorType catalogue; the only ErrorType example is 'not_found'.
limitations.impact: Lookup volume (several list calls per folder) and throttling behaviour are unknown, and mapping Horus 400s precisely to Chift 409/422/404 depends on ErrorType values Horus must provide.

limitations.description: partner_info carries only account_number (no description in the Chift spec, read as the company SearchKey, D10) and account_name. Companies created from it have no VAT number, no address, IsVatLiable=false, and the folder's language and country.
limitations.impact: A wrong reading of account_number would create or reuse the wrong third party. Companies created this way need completing in Horus Office; calling Create client/supplier first is the reliable path.
limitations.label: A

edge_cases.case: customer_refund or supplier_refund sent with negative amounts (Chift does not state the input sign)
edge_cases.handling: Normalise to absolute values and send Type=1. Reject mixed-sign lines that cannot be represented; send negative lines only once Horus confirms they are allowed.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Header totals ≠ sum of lines (rounding by the invoicing tool)
edge_cases.handling: Generate an invoice_correction line (Δ base and Δ tax, with the correction account and tax code). Without invoice_correction, reject 422, because Horus requires header = sum of lines.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: VAT computed at invoice level, so a line's tax_amount differs from base × rate by more than 1 cent
edge_cases.handling: Send OverrideTaxAmounts=true so Horus keeps the amounts provided. Otherwise Horus recalculates and only adapts within 1 cent.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Analytic split 33/33/34 on an amount that is not divisible
edge_cases.handling: Largest-remainder rounding on the per-line product allocation (D8): floor each row to the cent and give the remaining cents to the largest remainders (e.g. 0.10 → 0.03/0.03/0.04), so the CostLines sum exactly to BaseAmount.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Two plans each split, e.g. Dept A 50 / B 50 and Project X 30 / Y 70
edge_cases.handling: Four CostLines: A-X 15%, A-Y 35%, B-X 15%, B-Y 35% of BaseAmount (product, independence assumption). Document this behaviour for clients.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Line without analytic_distribution while a cost schema is Mandatory, or folder WithAnalytics=false while a distribution is sent
edge_cases.handling: Pre-check against cost-schemas.list Mandatory and folders.info WithAnalytics, and reject with a clear message. Horus behaviour is otherwise undocumented.

edge_cases.case: More than 8 analytic plans, or a plan id that is not a Horus cost schema
edge_cases.handling: Reject 422. Horus allows at most 8 schemas per folder.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Timeout or Horus 500 on the create call
edge_cases.handling: Never retry blindly (D12): Horus has no idempotency key and no invoice delete. First re-run the book-entries.list pre-check on DaybookId + DocumentNo (+ CompanyId); unconfirmed entries are included by default. If found, return the existing entry or 409. Otherwise retry with exponential backoff (Guide: Responses & errors). For a draft with Number=0, duplicates cannot be detected reliably, so do not auto-retry; surface the error. GET /book-entries.info cannot replace the pre-check here, because a timed-out create returns no Id.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: invoice_number non-numeric, e.g. 'F2024-001'
edge_cases.handling: Reject 422, or strip it to digits only if Chift accepts that policy. The original string must not be appended freely to Comment, which is reserved for the D3 reference | customer_memo convention; it can be carried only as reference when reference is empty.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Posted sale invoice without invoice_number
edge_cases.handling: Compute max(DocumentNo)+1 for the daybook and fiscal year, or reject and require a number. This carries a race risk, and the Horus numbering pattern is unknown (examples 201909001 / 1904001 / 202409001).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: No journal_id and several daybooks of the D1 candidate type (e.g. two 200 daybooks for a customer_invoice, or no 250 and two 200 daybooks for a customer_refund)
edge_cases.handling: Reject 400 'journal_id required' (D1; Chift rule: "otherwise, an error will be thrown").
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: invoice_date in a closed period, a closed fiscal year, or outside any fiscal year
edge_cases.handling: Pre-check, as Horus recommends, with fiscal-years.list closure dates (LastSalesClosureDate/LastPurchasesClosureDate/LastVatClosureDate; IncludeFuture for future years) and fiscal-years.info IsClosed. Reject with an explicit message.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Currency not in the Horus CurrencyCode enum (e.g. AED)
edge_cases.handling: Reject 422 before calling Horus (the enum is documented).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Foreign currency on a folder that is not configured for currencies
edge_cases.handling: No API field allows a pre-check. Expect a Horus 400 and pass its Details through (the exact Horus behaviour is undocumented).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: currency='EUR' with currency_exchange_rate=1
edge_cases.handling: CurrencyCode=null, CurrencyRate=null (null = EUR).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: PDF present but pdf_name missing or without an extension
edge_cases.handling: Default FileName to '<number>.pdf', or append '.pdf'; FileName with its extension is required when a document is attached.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Attachment that is not one of the supported types (e.g. .docx)
edge_cases.handling: Reject 422 before calling. Supported types are Pdf, Xml, CODA, SODA, .jpg/.jpeg/.png. File size cannot be pre-checked because no limit is documented.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: PDF attached in a second call (fallback) fails after the entry was created
edge_cases.handling: Prefer the single multipart call. In the fallback, return the created id with attachments_info.status='no' plus a warning, or retry book-entries.documents.new (which fails if a document already exists). Before any retry, check GET /book-entries.info → Document: if it is not null, the first attach succeeded and must not be retried. The entry cannot be rolled back.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Partner exists but IsCustomer=false for a sale (or IsSupplier=false for a purchase)
edge_cases.handling: partner_info flow (D10): set the missing flag with companies.update (CompanyId + flag only, never "" values). partner_id flow: the same flag update is the closest consistent behaviour (or reject, per Chift policy). Whether Horus refuses an invoice for a company without the flag is undocumented.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: OSS distance sale (TaxOrigin 13) without a country
edge_cases.handling: Under D2 an OSS sales code always carries its country (S-{TaxRate}-13-{TaxType}-{TaxCountryCode}), so TaxCountryCode comes from the code. An OSS id without the country component is not a catalogue id: reject 422. shipping_country is only a cross-check (warn when it differs).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Purchase on an account that requires a vehicle, or has a personal share (accounts HasPersonalShare)
edge_cases.handling: VehicleId and PersonalShare stay null because Chift has no source (an optional per-consumer default vehicle is possible). Whether Horus applies defaults or rejects is undocumented.

edge_cases.case: regroup_lines=true with different descriptions on merged lines
edge_cases.handling: Concatenate the descriptions (truncated). The response echoes the regrouped lines actually booked.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Line-level read-back (account-histories.list) finds no lines because Horus booked a different accounting month than invoice_date
edge_cases.handling: The header read-back is unaffected, because GET /book-entries.info takes only the Id. For the account-histories.list add-on, query the whole fiscal year with Filter.BookEntryId. If it still returns nothing, fall back to GET /account-histories.info for each AccountHistories[].Id from book-entries.info, which needs no period.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Read-back on a folder that is not VAT liable or has no analytics module
edge_cases.handling: VatDetail comes back null when the folder is not VAT liable, and CostDetail null when the folder has no analytics. Fall back to the echoed values.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: Analytic account maps to a cost section that is inactive or locked (IsLocked=true)
edge_cases.handling: Inactive sections are in the D8 cache (IncludeInactive = true) and are rejected with 422 'analytic account inactive'. For IsLocked sections, either reject or pass through and surface Horus's error; the behaviour is undocumented.

edge_cases.case: lines[].account_number is a summary (IsSummary=true) or collective account (e.g. 400000, IntCategory COLLECCUS)
edge_cases.handling: Pre-validate with accounts.list and reject with 422, since Chift requires a general account (assumption: Horus does not accept summary accounts on invoice lines).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Access token expires in the middle of the multi-call flow, or one consumer pushes several invoices in parallel
edge_cases.handling: Refresh proactively before expiry. On a 401, refresh once under a per-connection lock, persist the new pair before using it, then retry the failed call; for the create call, only after the DocumentNo pre-check. Parallel unserialised refreshes break the connection because refresh tokens are single-use.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: A company created from partner_info (IsVatLiable=false) is used with a reverse-charge or intra-EU tax combination (e.g. sales TaxOrigin 1 'Vente Cocontractant', TaxType 1 European)
edge_cases.handling: Warn, or reject when the decoded combination implies a VAT-liable counterparty. Recommend calling Create client/supplier with the VAT number first.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: companies.new in the partner_info flow hits an existing SearchKey that the exact-match post-filter missed (case difference, race)
edge_cases.handling: Expect a Horus 400. Re-query companies.list (exact SearchKey, same folder) and reuse the existing company, setting its role flag with companies.update if needed (D10). Duplicate-SearchKey behaviour is undocumented; only duplicate VAT numbers are documented as refused by default.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Connector testing and certification
edge_cases.handling: Run every .new call against a dedicated test license or test folder. Requests hit the license's real database, and test invoices cannot be deleted.
edge_cases.label: F

edge_cases.case: An invoice was pushed by mistake or twice
edge_cases.handling: No API delete exists for invoices. Report the duplicate to the client; the accountant must correct it in Horus Office.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Read-back fails after a successful create (GET /book-entries.info returns 404 or 500, or times out)
edge_cases.handling: Never re-create: the invoice exists, and Horus has no invoice delete. Return the Id with echoed values (last_updated_on null), log the failure, and retry the read-back later with backoff. A 404 right after a synchronous create is unexpected and should be reported to Horus.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: customer_refund (or supplier_refund) in a folder with no 250 (or 150) daybook
edge_cases.handling: D1 fallback: post with Type=1 into the single 200 (or 100) daybook. If Horus refuses a credit note in a Sale/Purchase daybook, surface the 400 and ask for a credit-note daybook or an explicit journal_id. get_invoices still finds the entry, because it scans both sibling daybook types and classifies each entry by the partner-line sign (D1).
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: journal_id of a daybook from another folder, or with a Type outside the invoice side (e.g. a 600 or a 100 daybook for a customer_invoice)
edge_cases.handling: Reject 400: the id is not in the folder's cached daybooks.list, or GET /daybooks.info → Data.Folder.Id ≠ folder_id (D13), or the Type is not 200/250 (customer_*) / 100/150 (supplier_*).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: partner_id of a company in another folder of the same license
edge_cases.handling: GET /companies.info → Data.Folder.Id ≠ folder_id → reject 400 before creating (D13). Horus's own behaviour on a cross-folder CompanyId is undocumented.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Analytic plan is a Free schema (CostSectionType 900), or a Free schema is Mandatory in the folder
edge_cases.handling: Reject 422: Free schemas are excluded from Chift analytics in v1 (D8). If a Free schema is Mandatory, lines cannot satisfy it through the connector; what Horus does with a missing mandatory value is undocumented, so surface Horus's error and keep the open question.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: Only customer_memo is set, or reference contains ' | '
edge_cases.handling: Memo only → Comment '| {customer_memo}' (D3); read routes must treat a leading '| ' as reference = null, because a split on ' | ' alone would not match it. A reference containing ' | ' would split wrongly on read: replace the separator inside the reference or reject it (connector policy).
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Foreign-currency invoice created with ignore_accounting_id=true
edge_cases.handling: Return the echoed invoice-currency amounts with the echoed currency (D4). main_currency_total = null, because the EUR partner-line amount needs a read-back. Never pair EUR amounts with the foreign code.
edge_cases.label: D

edge_cases.case: Company created from partner_info in a folder whose Language is 'XX'
edge_cases.handling: Send LanguageCode = 'XX' as-is (D9 write-side fallback). Whether companies.new accepts 'XX' on write is undocumented; on a Horus 400, surface the error.
edge_cases.label: A

edge_cases.case: status = posted while the consumer has the 'always push unconfirmed' setting on
edge_cases.handling: Send Confirmed=false (D12) and return status 'draft', the actual Horus state, so the client is not told the entry is final.
edge_cases.label: D

open_questions.question: Can a credit note (Type 1) be posted into a 200/100 daybook, and an invoice into 250/150? For credit notes, must amounts be positive?
open_questions.why: The D1 auto-selection posts customer_refund into a 200 daybook (supplier_refund into 100) when the folder has no 250 (150) daybook. Neither the API reference nor the posting guide ties Type to a daybook type or states the sign.

open_questions.question: Is Number unique per daybook and fiscal year? Does invoices.*.new reject or flag a duplicate Number, and with which ErrorType? Is there an idempotency key or external reference for invoices, or a way to get the next free number of an invoice daybook? (AutoGenerateNumber exists only on miscellaneous operations, banks and financials. Documents expose Status '900: PossibleDuplicata' / '901: DuplicataNumber', which hints at duplicate detection on the document side only.)
open_questions.why: Needed for Chift's invoice_number idempotency and for auto-numbering of posted invoices.

open_questions.question: Please provide the accepted-combination files (Tax-combinations-sales.xlsx and Tax-combinations-purchases.xlsx). Is there an API endpoint, current or planned, that lists VAT codes or accepted tax combinations? Are the files versioned?
open_questions.why: The D2 synthetic VAT catalogue behind Chift GET vat-codes and lines[].tax_code is built from these files, which are not among the admissible sources.

ba_insights: In Horus, an 'invoice' is a façade over a book entry. invoices.*.new 'will then be converted into a book entry' and returns only the book entry Id. That Id must be the Chift invoice id everywhere (GET invoices, GET attachments document_id). Any update generates a NEW Id and deletes the attachment, so Horus itself advises reconciling on daybook + entry number.

Terminology map, established from the Horus docs:
- **Horus folder = Chift folder:** the accounting record of one company; one license holds many folders.
- **Horus company = Chift client/supplier:** one entity with IsCustomer/IsSupplier flags.
- **Daybook = journal:** its Type drives which endpoint you post to; it has a SearchKey such as VEN.
- **Account:** a ledger account referenced by its search key.
- **Cost schema = analytic plan; cost section = analytic account.**
- **Confirmed:** validated by the accountant.
- **MatchNo:** the matching (lettering) number, NOT the invoice number, so matching.next-number.* must never be used for invoice numbering.

Why multi-call: Horus's own posting guide lists four prerequisites before posting an invoice: FolderId, the DaybookId of a 200/250 or 100/150 daybook, the CompanyId 'found or created', and the account search keys. One Chift call therefore becomes 1 create, 1 duplicate pre-check (whenever invoice_number is supplied, D12) and 0-2 read-back calls per invoice (usually just GET /book-entries.info by Id), plus reference lookups cached per folder (daybooks, accounts, the D8 analytics cache, fiscal years) and a cached companies.info folder guard per partner (D13). With a warm cache that is 2-3 Horus calls per invoice, 4 when line-level data is needed, and 1-2 more on the first invoice for a partner_info company (companies.list, then companies.update or companies.new).

Biggest trap: VAT. Chift assumes the target has VAT-code records with ids. Horus has none: it expects a combination of enums (rate + origin + type, plus kind/condition/value for purchases) checked against external tables. The connector must own a synthetic VAT-code catalogue with one id grammar shared by GET vat-codes, this route and get_invoices (D2): 'S-21-0-0' for a national 21% sale, 'P-21-2-0-0-1-true' for a deductible 21% purchase of merchandise. That makes GET vat-codes a hard dependency of invoice creation even though it is not in the case's list.

Second trap: analytics. Chift sends independent per-plan percentages. Horus stores amount rows that each combine one section per schema, i.e. a joint distribution. One plan converts exactly. Several split plans need a product, which assumes independence. Rounding uses the largest-remainder method so the cost lines sum exactly to the line's BaseAmount (D8). Chift ids are cost schema / cost section GUIDs, resolved to search keys from one per-folder cache that includes inactive sections, and Free schemas are out of scope in v1 (D8).

Numbering, idempotency and retries: Horus Number is numeric and required for sales ('can be 0 if not confirmed'). Invoices have no auto-number flag, Horus documents no uniqueness or external key, and there is NO invoice delete. Chift's recommended idempotency on invoice_number must therefore be emulated with a book-entries.list DocumentNo pre-check whenever invoice_number is supplied, surfaced as 409 (D12). The same pre-check must run before any retry after a 500 or timeout, because a duplicate cannot be undone through the API.

Status mapping is technically trivial (posted → Confirmed=true) but has documented business weight. Horus keeps API entries unconfirmed by default 'which lets the accountant review them'. D12 keeps posted → Confirmed=true but adds a per-consumer 'always push unconfirmed' setting, recommended for fiduciary clients; the response then says 'draft'. Which default to ship is a product decision to agree with Chift and Horus.

Use the multipart variant whenever a PDF is present: the invoice and its document are created in one call. File types are documented (Pdf, Xml, CODA, SODA, jpg/jpeg/png); size is not. The two-step fallback (JSON create, then book-entries.documents.new) can leave an entry without its PDF, and that cannot be rolled back.

Sales and purchases differ even though one Chift route covers both. Purchases add TaxKind/TaxCondition/TaxConditionValue (deductibility), VehicleId and PersonalShare, and Number is nullable. Sales add TaxCountryCode for OSS. The tax-code decoder and validation must branch on invoice_type.

Response strategy: most of InvoiceItemOutMultiAnalyticPlans can be echoed from the validated request plus the resolved ids (partner, daybook). Pick the cheapest correct source per field. GET /book-entries.info, one call by Id with no period (folder-checked, D13), gives last_updated_on, status, DocumentNo (needed when a purchase was sent without a number), header totals and the document link. Currency (D4): amounts are the echoed invoice-currency amounts with the echoed currency, and EUR amounts (CompanyDetail, Debit/Credit) are never paired with a foreign code. Only the EUR partner-line amount (main_currency_total) of a foreign-currency invoice, the partner collective account and booked line VAT/cost detail need the period-bounded account-histories.list (Filter.BookEntryId over the fiscal year), so add it only when one of those is required. Skip all read-backs when ignore_accounting_id=true; Horus is synchronous, so the id is still returned.

Operational hygiene from the guides:
- Refresh tokens are single-use, so serialise refreshes per connection and persist the new pair before use.
- Handle errors as Horus prescribes: 401 → refresh once and retry; 400 → do not retry, surface Details; 500 → back off.
- Send gzip.
- Ignore unknown response properties, because Horus adds properties without notice.
- Test only on a test license or folder, because the API works on real data.

Horus is BE/LU only (Legislation enum). That explains why nl_payment_terms_split and withholding_tax have no counterpart, and why the TaxOrigin labels are Belgian/Luxembourgish categories. Present these as market-scope limitations, not connector gaps.

Write for the round trip (D1, D2, D3): what this route writes must be readable by get_invoices. Refunds that fall back to a 200/100 daybook are still found, because get_invoices scans both sibling daybook types and classifies each entry by the partner-line sign. The D2 grammar lets get_invoices re-encode tax codes from VatDetail (except purchase codes that differ only by TaxKind, which read back as null). The D3 Comment convention ('{reference} | {customer_memo}') lets reference and customer_memo be parsed back, once Horus confirms where the header Comment surfaces on read.

partner_info is a Chift field without a description (D10). The connector reads account_number as the Horus company SearchKey and runs find → set role flag → create, never overwriting other company fields (companies.update with null, not "", for everything except the flag). Present it to clients as a convenience fallback: the reliable path is Create client/supplier first, then partner_id.

Folder scoping (D7, D13): one Horus license holds many folders and Id-only calls carry no FolderId. folder_id is required as soon as the connection has more than one selected folder, and every Id-only lookup (companies.info, daybooks.info, book-entries.info) checks Data.Folder.Id, so an id from another folder can never be posted or returned by mistake.
